name: Lying and Deceit

counsel.text: The heart and tongue should go together, as the dial goes exactly with the sun. To speak fair to one's face, and not to mean what one speaks, is no better than a lie.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, the truth of God

counsel.text: If ever thou wilt mortify thy corruptions, thou must tie up thy conscience to the law, shut it from all shifts and exceptions, until it owns its guilt with a clear and thorough apprehension; so that thence, as David speaks, thy "iniquity may ever be before thee."
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: Lying is a sin that does not go alone; it ushers in other sins. Absalom told his father a lie, when he said that he was going to pay his vow at Hebron, and this was a preface to his treason.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: It is the Spirit alone that can do, that doth, this work to the purpose. And this is the first thing that the Spirit doth in order to the mortification of any lust whatever, -- it convinces the soul of all the evil of it, cuts off all its pleas, discovers all its deceits, stops all its evasions, answers its pretences, makes the soul own its abomination, and lie down under the sense of it.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: When thou speakest, let thy word be as authentic as thy oath. Imitate God, who is the pattern of truth.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: By a lie in our words we deny the truth; by a lie in our profession we disgrace it.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, the truth of God

counsel.text: Hypocrisy is a lie with a fair cover over it. An insincere heart is a half heart. The inward frame and motion of the heart comports not with the profession and behaviour of the outward man, like a clock, whose wheels within go not as the hand points without.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: The more subtle thou seemest in concealing thy sin, the more egregiously thou playest the fool. None so shamed as the liar when found out, and that thou art sure to be. Thy covering is too short to hide thee from God's eye, and what God sees, if thou dost not put thyself to shame, he will tell all the world hereafter, however thou escapest in this life.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: Though the serpent can shrink up into his folds, and appear what he is not, yet it doth not become the saints to juggle or shuffle with God or men; and truly when any of them have made use of the serpent's subtlety, it hath not followed their hand. Jacob got the blessing by a wile, but he might have had it cheaper with plain dealing.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: As you love your peace, Christians, be plain-hearted with God and man, and keep the king's highway. Go the plain way of command to obtain thy desire, and not leap over hedge and ditch to come a little sooner to the journey's end; such commonly either meet with some stop that makes them come back with shame, or else put to venture their necks in some desperate leap.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: There are, as Augustine says, two sorts of lies. An officious lie, when a man tells a lie for his profit; as, when a tradesman says his commodity cost him so much, when perhaps it did not cost him half so much. He that will lie in his trade shall lie in hell. A jesting lie, when a man tells a lie in sport, to make others merry, and goes laughing to hell. He who tells a lie makes himself like the devil.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, the truth of God

counsel.text: A man may wrong another as well by silence as by slander, when he knows him to be wrongfully accused, yet does not speak in his behalf. If others cast false aspersions on any, we should wipe them off.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: God of truth, you cannot lie, and lying lips are an abomination to you. I come through Jesus Christ, who is the truth. I confess that I have lied. I have told outright lies, half-truths, and exaggerations. I have hidden what I should have confessed, and I have deceived to protect myself or to look better than I am. Behind my lies is a heart that fears people more than you, and loves its own reputation more than your glory. In this I have imitated the father of lies and not my Father in heaven. I have broken trust with others and grieved your Spirit. Forgive me, Lord. Christ was condemned by false witnesses and kept silent; he bore the punishment for my deceit. For his sake pardon me, and give me courage to make things right with those I have deceived. Holy Spirit, put this falsehood to death, and make me truthful in the inward being. Let my yes be yes and my no be no. I thank you that in Christ I am fully known and fully forgiven, so I no longer need to hide. In his name. Amen.

prayers.title: When I am tempted to lie
prayers.text: Lord, I am about to bend the truth to protect myself. Stop me before I speak. You see everything already; there is nothing I can hide from you. Give me courage to tell the truth even if it costs me. Remind me that I have put off the old self with its practices, and have put on the new self, created after your likeness in true righteousness and holiness. Lord Jesus, you are the truth; let me speak as your disciple. Holy Spirit, give me honest words now. Amen.

prayers.title: For a truthful heart
prayers.text: Father, you desire truth in the inward being. Make me honest with you, with myself, and with others. Free me from the fear of man and the love of praise that tempt me to deceive. Teach me to confess my faults plainly, to keep my promises even when they hurt, and to speak the truth in love. Let me be someone others can trust, so that my life honors the God of truth. Through Jesus Christ. Amen.

prayers.title: Confessing deceit
prayers.text: And if in any thing we have gone beyond and defrauded our brother, if we have walked with vanity, and our foot hath hasted to deceit, and any blot hath cleaved to our hands, Lord, discover it to us, that if we have done iniquity, we may do so no more.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

prayers.title: For simplicity and godly sincerity
prayers.text: O that we may always have our conversation in the world in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God! Lord, uphold us in our integrity, and set us before thy face for ever, and let integrity and uprightness preserve us, for we wait on thee. Let our hearts be sound in thy statutes, that we be not ashamed; and let our eye be single, that our whole body may be full of light.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

examinationQuestions: When you were tempted to shade the truth today, what were you afraid of: blame, losing face, or losing something you wanted?
Have you been trusting a lie to protect you more than you have trusted God to keep you?
Did you leave anyone with a false picture today, through silence, a half-truth, or exaggeration?
Is there a lie you have told that still stands? What would it take to set it right?
Are you living one way before others and another way before God?
Are you being honest with yourself about this sin, or are you making excuses for it?
fleeActions: Stop before you answer. Then say only what is true, even if your answer is short.
If you have just told a lie, go back now and correct it. Say plainly what you said and what is really true.
Do not send the message or sign the form until every word in it is true.
Tell a brother or sister in your church about the lie you are tempted to keep, so that it is brought into the light.
Open your Bible to Psalm 32, read it, and confess the matter to God out loud.
Write down what you fear will happen if you tell the truth, then pray and give that fear to God.

afterFallReadings.text: Christ by his intercession answers all bills of indictment brought in against the elect. Do what they can, sin, and then Satan, accuses believers to God, and conscience accuses them to themselves; but Christ, by his intercession, answers all these accusations.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's priestly office
